column1: # Official media to fetch from the Internet Archive and, when asked, extract
# name <TAB> archive.org item <TAB> file pattern <TAB> corpus output dir <TAB> action [<TAB> exclude regex]
# A push that changes this file starts .github/workflows/import-media.yml,
# which fetches every entry that is not fetched yet, inventories it, and
# imports the documentation pages of the entries whose action is `import`
# or `import-scratch`; already fetched media is never downloaded twice and an
# already extracted component is skipped.
#   inventory        download (if needed) + list what the medium holds
#   import           ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is kept verbatim under sources/<name>/ with a
#                    PROVENANCE.md
#   import-scratch   ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is fetched to .cache/media/ and thrown away again
#                    (an InstallShield-era installer disc is ~40 MB of mostly
#                    binaries and samples - the corpus keeps pages, not media)
#   inventory-scratch
#                    download and list what the medium holds, then throw the
#                    medium away: for a disc that is only being considered
# A finished import is recorded in data/reports/media-imported.tsv, so a later
# run does not download an image it has already imported (the scratch medium is
# gone by then); `--force` overrides it.
# Either way only documentation is imported: this is a documentation corpus,
# so a medium's source files, headers, samples and toolchains are counted in
# the inventory and skipped (see "What is collected" in the top-level README).
# The 6th field refuses documentation files that are not documentation of the
# product: the exclude below drops infoview.hlp, the SDK disc's 1,236-page help
# for the InfoViewer/Visual C++ viewer UI itself (dialog boxes, wizard fields,
# editor options).  It is Microsoft help, but it is not Windows CE material.
# windbg.hlp (the CE debugger reference) and the disc's readme stay.
# windows-ce-2.0-sdk: Microsoft Windows CE Platform SDK (H/PC) 2.0 (02/98) -
# the CE 2.0 SDK whose Books Online the corpus has been looking for since the
# CE 2.0 Technical Information CD turned out to carry no API reference (see
# sources/windows-ce-2.0/PROVENANCE.md).  The disc is an InstallShield
# installer: the documentation is inside data1.cab/_sys1.cab, which the
# workflow unpacks with `unshield` (7z cannot read InstallShield cabinets).
# The first import attempt downloaded and inventoried the disc but imported
# nothing (7z cannot read those cabinets, and the inventory then crashed on the
# extensionless files of the disc - fixed in tools/import-media.py).
windows-ce-2.0-sdk
# The DevCon '99 conference CD (1999): the Windows CE Developers Conference
# disc.  338 MB / 1,689 files; the inventory found 843 HTML pages, 37 CHMs and
# 3 WinHelp books among the sessions, and the rest is the conference's samples
# and toolchain (1,082 .h, 945 .cpp, 115 .dsp, ...) which stays out.
wcedevcon-99
